 Advertisement Rahm Emanuel visits Exeter to speak with NH Democrats
 Advertisement Updated: 6:38 PM EDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ricky Podgorski Reporter Rahm Emanuel visits Exeter to speak with NH Democrats
 Updated: 6:38 PM EDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ricky Podgorski Reporter EXETER, N.H. — Former White House chief of staff, Chicago mayor and ambassador to Japan Rahm Emanuel was back in New Hampshire Sunday, rallying canvassers ahead of the midterm election.
 Emanuel has been rumored to be considering a potential 2028 presidential campaign, but he says his focus right now is helping local Democrats in the primaries.
 Advertisement "Don't worry about me. I'm good. I get to come out here and see these beautiful fall-colored leaves. Don't worry about it," Emanuel said. "You got this election. Focus on this election and then focus on bringing change."
 The last time Emanuel was in New Hampshire, he biked from Portsmouth to Hanover, connecting with Granite Staters along the way in June. 
 He spoke in Exeter today, rallying canvassers before they hit the streets to talk with voters about Democratic candidates, including Chris Pappas and Stefany Shaheen.
 "The American people are going to be the thin blue line that protects this country," Emanuel told the crowd.
 One canvasser said Emanuel inspired her.
 "I'm only this one person in Exeter doing this in New Hampshire, and it gave me that more global perspective that across the country, people are mobilizing and it is momentum," Bernadette Murphy, of Exeter, said.
 Emanuel took aim at the Trump administration, calling it corrupt and criticizing its efforts on affordability.
 "He's fixated on his arch, and American families can't afford to eat at the Golden Arches," Emanuel said.
 He urged canvassers to keep talking to their neighbors and make sure voters know who's on the ballot.
 "You got a great candidate for Senate, and you got a great congressional candidate. Yes, yes, you have great state legislative races. Don't you leave a neighbor un-talked to, a neighbor not discussed or somebody you don't know," Emanuel said. "They're all running great races, but you got to, you got to basically don't spike the ball on the 10-yard line."
